for we are responsible solely for the sighting on the night of the thirtieth;
וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאוּ לֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד — אֵין לָחוּשׁ, דְּ"לֹא רְאִינוּ" אֵין רְאָיָה;
and as for the fact that they did not see it on the night of the thirty-first — there is no concern, for "we have not seen" is not halakhic proof;
וְהַבֵּית דִּין מְקַדְּשִׁים יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים כְּעֵדוּת הָעֵדִים, וְאֵין לָהֶם לָחוּשׁ כְּלָל:
and the court sanctifies the thirtieth day based on the testimony of the witnesses, having no concern at all.
וּלְפִיכָךְ בֵּית דִּין עַצְמָם, שֶׁרָאוּ בְּלֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים
Therefore, if the court itself sighted [the new moon] on the night of the thirtieth —
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרְאִיַּת הַבֵּית דִּין עַצְמָם אֵינָהּ פְּחוּתָה מִשְּׁמִיעַת דִּבְרֵי הָעֵדִים
even though the sighting by the court itself is not inferior to hearing the testimony of witnesses —

nevertheless, since they sighted it at night, at a time when they are not qualified to hold court,
אִם כֵּן לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים אָז לַעֲשׂוֹת דִּין,
consequently they were not able at that time to enact judgment,
וְיִצְטָרְכוּ לְקַדֵּשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ בַּיּוֹם עַל פִּי רְאִיָּתָם בַּלַּיְלָה;
and they would have to sanctify subsequently during the day based on their night sighting;
וְאֵין רְאִיָּתָם אֶלָּא כְּעֵדוּת, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לְקַדְּשׁוֹ תֵּכֶף לִרְאִיָּה,
and their sighting is considered merely as testimony, since they could not sanctify it immediately upon sighting,
וְקַיְימָא לַן [וְקַיָּם לָנוּ] אֵין עֵד נַעֲשֶׂה דַּיָּן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
and we hold the principle that a witness cannot become a judge, as will be clarified in its place.
לְפִיכָךְ צְרִיכִים לְהוֹשִׁיב עוֹד שְׁנַיִם אֲחֵרִים אֵצֶל אֶחָד מֵהֶם,

and the two [original judges] shall testify before the three on the thirtieth day, and the three shall sanctify it.
אֲבָל אִם רָאוּ בְּיוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים, הוֹאִיל וְהוּא זְמַן קִדּוּשׁ — מְקַדְּשִׁין בְּעַצְמָם
However, if they sighted it during the day of the thirtieth, since it is a valid time for sanctification — they sanctify it themselves

(see the Commentator, who left this unresolved because he was unaware of the distinction here;

and with due respect to his honor, the distinction is clear in the Talmud, as mentioned).
וְאִם רָאוּ סָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה שֶׁל יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיקוּ לוֹמַר "מְקֻדָּשׁ" עַד שֶׁחֲשֵׁכָה
And if they sighted it close to sunset on the twenty-ninth day, and did not manage to proclaim "It is sanctified" before dark —
מְקַדְּשִׁים בְּיוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים עַל פִּי עַצְמָם, בְּלִי שֶׁיַּעֲמִידוּ עֵדִים;

כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאוּ בְּשָׁעָה הָרְאוּיָה לְקַדֵּשׁ, אֵין צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת עֵדִים וִיהֵא אֵין עֵד נַעֲשֶׂה דַּיָּן

And this applies specifically when it is impossible to reconcile their words, such as here;

However, if one says two statures and the other says three statures —

even where one says three and the other says five, we calculate according to the elevated position of the one saying three relative to the one saying five:
אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא עוֹמֵד בְּגֹבַהּ — יִהְיֶה נִרְאֶה נָמוּךְ קוֹמָה אַחַת, וּבְקוֹמָה אַחַת טָעוּ אִינָשֵׁי, וּמִצְטָרְפִים
it is possible that because he stood elevated, it appeared to him one stature lower, and within one stature people commonly err, so they combine
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ב׳, סוֹף הֲלָכָה ד׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם).
(Jerusalem Talmud Chapter 2, end of Halakhah 4, see there).
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה לְהֵפֶךְ: אִם אֶחָד אוֹמֵר אַרְבָּעָה וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ, וְהָיָה זֶה הָאוֹמֵר אַרְבָּעָה עוֹמֵד בְּגֹבַהּ מֵהָאוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ
And the reverse also seems true: if one says four and one says three, and the one saying four stood elevated above the one saying three —
אֵין מִצְטָרְפִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בֵּינֵיהֶם אֶלָּא קוֹמָה אַחַת:
they do not combine, even though the difference between their words is only one stature.
(וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן, כָּתַב דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּלְפִי גֹּבַהּ הַקּוֹמוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ אָדָם טוֹעֶה שְׁלִישׁ מִלְּבַר;
(And see there in Sefer Turei Even, who wrote that one might say that relative to the total height estimated, a person typically errs by one-third externally;
וּלְכָךְ בִּשְׁנַיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ מִצְטָרְפִים, דְּאִי שֶׁל שְׁנַיִם טָעָה — הֲוֵי שְׁלִישׁ מִלְּבַר לִפְחוֹת, וְאִי שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ טָעָה — הֲוֵי שְׁלִישׁ מִלְּבַר לְהוֹסִיף.
and therefore at two and three statures they combine, for if the one who said two erred — it is an error of one-third less, and if the one who said three erred — it is an error of one-third more.
(אֵין דְּבָרָיו מְכֻוָּנִים: וּמֵאַיִן הוּא אוֹמֵר "הַשְּׁלִישׁ מִלְּבַר"?
(Yet his words are not exact: from where does he assert "one-third externally"?
אִם מֵהָאֻמְדָּנָא — נִיחָא אִי בַּעַל שָׁלֹשׁ טָעָה; אֲבָל אִי שֶׁל שְׁנַיִם טָעָה — הֲוֵי שְׁלִישׁ מִלְּגָאו.
If derived from the true height — it works well if the one saying three erred; but if the one saying two erred — it is one-third internally.
וְאִי מֵהַטָּעוּת שְׁלִישׁ — אִם כֵּן נִיחָא אִי שֶׁל שְׁנַיִם טָעָה, אִי שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ טָעָה — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר.)
And if one-third of the estimate itself — then it works if the one saying two erred, but if the one saying three erred — what can be said?).
וּלְפִי זֶה בְּאֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר חֲמִשָּׁה — דַּוְקָא חֲמִשָּׁה, הָא אַרְבָּעָה וָחֵצִי טָעֵי אִינָשֵׁי בִּשְׁלִישׁ.
And according to this, when one says three and the other says five — it is specifically five that invalidates, whereas at four and a half people can still err by a third.
וְהַדַּעַת נוֹטָה כֵּן, דְּוַדַּאי נִתְרַבָּה הַטָּעוּת לְפִי רִבּוּי הַגֹּבַהּ, עַד כָּאן.
And reason leans toward this, for certainly the margin of error increases with greater height; thus far his words.
וּקְצָת רְאָיָה לִדְבָרָיו מֵהַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי (פֶּרֶק ב׳ סוֹף הֲלָכָה ד׳):
And partial support for his view emerges from the Jerusalem Talmud (Chapter 2, end of Halakhah 4):
בְּזֶה אוֹמֵר מְלֹא מַרְדֵּעַ אַחַת וְזֶה אוֹמֵר מְלֹא שְׁנֵי מַרְדְּעִים — אֵין דִּבְרֵיהֶם קַיָּמִים בְּעוֹמְדִים בְּשָׁוֶה.
where this one says the length of one ox-goad and that one says the length of two ox-goads — their words do not stand when standing on level ground.
וְקָשֶׁה, הָא אָדָם טוֹעֶה מְלֹא מַרְדֵּעַ אַחַת!
And this is difficult: does not a person normally err by the length of one ox-goad?!
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּדַוְקָא בִּשְׁלִישׁ — לֹא בְּזֶה אוֹמֵר אֶחָד וְזֶה אוֹמֵר שְׁנַיִם.
Perforce it must be as mentioned above, that error is granted specifically within one-third — not when one says one and the other says two.
מִיהוּ יִתָּכֵן דְּהַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי פָּלִיג אַתַּלְמוּדִין):
(However, it is quite possible that the Jerusalem Talmud disagrees with our Babylonian Talmud).
וְעֵדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ "רְאִינוּהוּ בְּלֹא כַּוָּנָה, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִתְבּוֹנַנּוּ בּוֹ וְנִתְכַּוַּנּוּ לִרְאוֹתוֹ לְהָעִיד — שׁוּב לֹא רְאִינוּהוּ" — אֵין זוֹ עֵדוּת;
And witnesses who said, "We saw it unintentionally, but when we focused upon it and intended to view it to bear testimony — we no longer saw it" — this is not valid testimony;
שֶׁמָּא עָבִים נִתְקַשְּׁרוּ, וְנִרְאוּ כִּלְבָנָה, וְהָלְכוּ לָהֶם:
for perhaps clouds gathered, appearing like the crescent moon, and then dispersed.
וְעֵדִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁרָאוּ יָרֵחַ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע — אֵין שׁוֹמְעִים לָהֶם,
And witnesses who asserted that they sighted the moon on the twenty-ninth — we do not listen to them,
שֶׁאֵין חֲדָשָׁה שֶׁל לְבָנָה פָּחוֹת מֵעֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע יוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל;
for the renewal cycle of the moon is never less than twenty-nine days, as explained above;
אֶלָּא הַיְשָׁנָה רָאוּ, אוֹ דְּמוּת לְבָנָה בֶּעָבִים.
rather, they saw the old moon, or an optical illusion of a moon among the clouds.
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אִם אָמְרוּ אוֹתָם עֵדִים שֶׁרָאוּהָ בְּשַׁחֲרִית, קֹדֶם עֲלוֹת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע בַּמִּזְרָח,
Nonetheless, if those same witnesses said that they saw it at dawn, prior to sunrise, on the twenty-ninth in the east,
וּרְאוּהוּ עַרְבִית אַחַר שְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה בַּמַּעֲרָב
and saw it at evening after sunset in the west [on the thirtieth] —
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁתֵּרָאֶה הַיְשָׁנָה שַׁחֲרִית וְהַחֲדָשָׁה עַרְבִית,
and even though it is physically impossible for the old moon to be seen at dawn and the new at dusk,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְמַעְלָה שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בֵּינֵיהֶם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע שָׁעָה
and as I wrote above that at the very least twenty-four hours must elapse between them —
אוֹמְרִים שֶׁדְּמוּת לְבָנָה רָאוּ בְּשַׁחֲרִית מֵעָבִים, וּמְקַדְּשִׁין עַל רְאִיָּה זוֹ שֶׁרָאוּ בִּשְׁלוֹשִׁים;
we say that they merely saw the illusion of a moon at dawn from clouds, and we sanctify based on this sighting they had on the thirtieth;
וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים שֶׁמָּא גַּם זוֹ הָיְתָה מֵעָבִים
and we do not suspect that this evening sighting was likewise from clouds

(see the Commentary on the Mishnah by Rambam, who seemingly explains like Rashi;

yet see Rabbi Ovadiah of Bartenura and Tosafot Yom Tov in what they wrote: "and it is hidden in the light of the sun for approximately two days," etc. —
נִרְאֶה דִּמְפָרֵשׁ כְּרַבּוֹתָיו דְּרַשִׁ״י;
it appears he interprets like the teachers of Rashi;
וּלְפִי פֵּרוּשָׁם דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִלְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי — נִיחָא קֻשְׁיַת רַשִׁ״י עֲלֵיהֶם.
and according to their explanation that Rabban Gamliel referred to a distinct tradition — Rashi's difficulty against them is resolved.
אֲבָל מֵהַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת (דַּף כ״ד עַמּוּד ב׳) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "רְאִינוּהוּ",
Yet from the Jerusalem Talmud cited by Tosafot (folio 24b) s.v. "Re'inuhu,"
שֶׁכָּתַב "וְלָמָּה קִבְּלָהּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? שֶׁכֵּן מְסֹרֶת" וְכוּלֵי — לֹא מַשְׁמַע כֵּן, וְיְעֻיַּן שָׁם בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי עַצְמוֹ).
which wrote "And why did Rabban Gamliel accept it? Because such was a tradition," etc. — it is not indicated as such, and let the Jerusalem Talmud itself be consulted there).
וְכֵן אִם רָאוּהוּ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, וּבְלֵיל עִבּוּרוֹ לֹא נִרְאָה — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ נֶאֱמָנִים,
And likewise if they saw it in its proper time [the thirtieth], and on the night of its intercalation [the thirty-first] it was not visible — they are believed,
שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ אַחְרָאִים אֶלָּא לִרְאִיַּת לֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים בִּלְבַד;
for we are responsible solely for the sighting on the night of the thirtieth;
וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאוּ לֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד — אֵין לָחוּשׁ, דְּ"לֹא רְאִינוּ" אֵין רְאָיָה;
and as for the fact that they did not see it on the night of the thirty-first — there is no concern, for "we have not seen" is not halakhic proof;
וְהַבֵּית דִּין מְקַדְּשִׁים יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים כְּעֵדוּת הָעֵדִים, וְאֵין לָהֶם לָחוּשׁ כְּלָל:
and the court sanctifies the thirtieth day based on the testimony of the witnesses, having no concern at all.
אֵין הָעֵדִים הוֹלְכִים לְהָעִיד אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶם וּבֵין מְקוֹם הַבֵּית דִּין מַהֲלַךְ לַיְלָה וָיוֹם אוֹ פָּחוֹת.
The witnesses do not go to testify unless there is between them and the location of the court a distance of a night and a day’s journey or less.
(וְנִרְאֶה: דְּרָאוּ הַלְּבָנָה בִּתְחִלַּת לֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים;
(And it appears: this applies where they saw the moon at the beginning of the night of the thirtieth;
אֲבָל רָאוּהָ בִּתְחִלַּת יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים — צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַק מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם.
but if they saw it at the beginning of the day of the thirtieth — it must be only a day’s journey.
וְדַוְקָא אַחַר תַּקָּנַת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר לְהַלָּן, לְקַדֵּשׁ אַחַר הַמִּנְחָה;
And this is specifically after the enactment of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, as will be explained below, to sanctify after the afternoon offering [Minchah];
אֲבָל מִקַּמֵּי הָכֵי צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מֶרְחָק שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ לְבֵית דִּין קֹדֶם מִנְחָה, דְּאַחַר כָּךְ לֹא יְקַבְּלוּ עֵדוּתָם.)
(whereas prior to that, the distance needed to be such that they could reach the court before Minchah, for afterwards they would not accept their testimony).
אֲבָל הָיָה בֵּינֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר עַל כָּךְ — לֹא יֵלְכוּ לְהָעִיד, הוֹאִיל וּכְבָר נִתְעַבֵּר הַחֹדֶשׁ.
However, if there was between them more than that distance — they should not go to testify, since the month will already have become intercalated [thirty days].
וְאִם הָיָה בֵּינֵיהֶם מַהֲלָךְ הַנִּזְכָּר — הֲרֵי הֵם מְחַלְּלִים שַׁבָּת, אִם חָל בְּשַׁבָּת, לֵילֵךְ לְהָעִיד
And if the distance between them was the aforementioned journey — behold, they desecrate Shabbat, if it fell on Shabbat, to go and testify
(וַאֲפִלּוּ מַכְשִׁירֵי דָּחוּ שַׁבָּת).
((and even auxiliary preparations override Shabbat).
וַאֲפִלּוּ לֹא הָיָה נַפְקָא מִינָּהּ לְעִנְיַן קָרְבָּן — מְחַלְּלִין, דְּמִצְוָה לְקַדֵּשׁ עַל הָרְאִיָּה (דַּף כ׳ רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳).
(And even if there were no practical halakhic difference regarding sacrifices — they desecrate, for it is a mitzvah to sanctify upon the visual sighting (folio 20a).
וְעַיֵּן בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי הָרַשְׁבָּ״א [בְּרַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה בֶּן אַדֶּרֶת] (דַּף כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳) דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "עַל קְרִיאָתָן",
And see in the novellae of the Rashba (folio 21b) s.v. "Al Keri'atan,"

וְכֵן רַשָּׁאִים שְׁתֵּי כִּתֵּי עֵדִים לֵילֵךְ בְּיַחַד וּלְחַלֵּל שַׁבָּת, דִּשְׁמָּא תִּפָּסֵל כַּת אַחַת.
And likewise, two sets of witnesses are permitted to go together and desecrate Shabbat, lest one set be disqualified.
וְנִרְאֶה דִּכִתּוֹת הַרְבֵּה — וַדַּאי דְּאֵין רַשָּׁאִים, דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר דִּבְכָל הָנֵי לֹא יִמְצָא אַחַת הַכְּשֵׁרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְמַעְלָה אַדִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י בְּאַרְבָּעִים זוּג);

And it appears that many sets — are certainly not permitted, for it is impossible that among all of these not even one kosher set will be found (as I wrote above regarding Rashi’s words on the forty pairs);
אֶלָּא דִּלְפִי זֶה צָרִיךְ עִיּוּן: אִם כֵּן נָתַתָּ דְּבָרֶיךָ לְשִׁעוּרִים, וְאֵיזֶה נִקְרָא כִּתּוֹת הַרְבֵּה?
except that according to this it requires analysis: if so, you have made your words subject to arbitrary measurements, and what is considered "many sets"?
וְלָכֵן אֶפְשָׁר דִּבְכָל גַּוְנֵי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
Therefore, it is possible that in all cases it is entirely permissible.
וְאִם הָיָה הָעֵד שֶׁרָאָה אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ בְּלֵילֵי שַׁבָּת חוֹלֶה, שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לֵילֵךְ — מַרְכִּיבִין אוֹתוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר, וַאֲפִלּוּ בְּמִטָּה.
And if the witness who saw the new moon on Friday night was sick and unable to walk — they mount him upon a donkey, and even [carry him] in a bed.
וְאִם יֵשׁ לָהֶם אוֹרְבִים בַּדֶּרֶךְ מִן הַצְּדוֹקִים הָאֶפִּיקוֹרְסִים לְעַכֵּב הֲלִיכָתָם — לוֹקְחִין בְּיָדָם כְּלֵי זַיִן, אַף אוֹתָם שֶׁאָסְרוּ לְטַלְטְלָם בְּשַׁבָּת.
And if they have ambushers on the road from among the Sadducees and heretics to obstruct their travel — they take weapons in hand, even those whose handling is normally forbidden on Shabbat.
וְאִם הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה (כְּמַהֲלַךְ יוֹם וָלַיְלָה) — לוֹקְחִים בְּיָדָם מְזוֹנוֹת.
And if it was a distant journey (such as the travel of a day and a night) — they take provisions in hand.
(וְנִרְאֶה לִי: כָּל דְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ, אִם אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָם עַל יְדֵי עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים — וַדַּאי יַעֲשׂוּ עַל יָדוֹ, וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה;

(And it appears to me: all these things, if it is possible to perform them through a gentile — they must certainly do so through him, and not through an Israelite, since it is merely a preparatory measure for a mitzvah;
וּבְכָל עִנְיָן שֶׁיִּרְאֶה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַקְטִין הָאִסּוּר — מִדְּאוֹרַיְתָא לִדְרַבָּנָן, וְכַהַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל — וַדַּאי יַעֲשֶׂה):
(and in any circumstance where he sees he can diminish the severity of the prohibition — from biblical to rabbinic, as mentioned above — he must certainly do so).
וּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה לֹא הָיוּ זָזִין כָּל הַיּוֹם מִן הֶחָצֵר שֶׁבָּאוּ בּוֹ לְהָעִיד שָׁם, כְּדִין הַיּוֹצֵא לַתְּחוּם;
And initially, they would not move the entire day from the courtyard into which they had arrived to testify, according to the law of one who leaves the Shabbat boundary;
עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן וְהִתְקִין שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְהַלְּכִין אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִמָּנְעוּ מִלָּבוֹא;
until Rabban Gamliel the Elder came and enacted that they may walk two thousand cubits in every direction, so that they should not be deterred from coming;
וְכֵן בְּכָל יוֹצֵא בִּרְשׁוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
and likewise for anyone who ventures forth with permission, as will be explained in its place.
וּבְכָל עִנְיָן צְרִיכִים הָעֵדִים לֵילֵךְ לְהָעִיד בְּשַׁבָּת, בֵּין שֶׁרָאוּהוּ קָטָן בֵּין שֶׁרָאוּהוּ גָּדוֹל.
And in all circumstances the witnesses are required to go and testify on Shabbat, whether they saw [the crescent] small or whether they saw it large.
וְנִרְאֶה: לְכָל לֹא יֹאמְרוּ "כְּשֵׁם שֶׁרְאִינוּהוּ אֲנַחְנוּ, רָאוּהוּ אֲחֵרִים, וְאֵין אָנוּ צְרִיכִים לְחַלֵּל הַשַּׁבָּת";
And it appears: above all, they must not say, "Just as we saw it, others saw it, and we do not need to desecrate Shabbat";

אֶלָּא מְחַלְּלִים כָּל מִי שֶׁיִּרְאֶה הַלְּבָנָה, וְרָאוּי לְהָעִיד, וְיִהְיֶה בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין מְקוֹם הַבֵּית דִּין לַיְלָה וָיוֹם אוֹ פָּחוֹת — מִצְוָה עָלָיו לְחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֵילֵךְ לְהָעִיד.

rather, everyone who sees the moon and is qualified to testify, and the distance between him and the court’s location is a night and a day or less — it is a mitzvah upon him to desecrate the Shabbat and go to testify.
(נִרְאֶה לְטַעְמַאי: אֲפִלּוּ קָרוֹב מְאֹד לִמְקוֹם בֵּית דִּין, דִּשְׁמָּא שָׁם עָבִים כִּסּוּהָ וְלֹא נִרְאֵית.)
((According to my reasoning, it seems: even if he is very close to the court’s location, lest clouds covered it there and it was not seen).
וְנִרְאֶה לִי: אִם בַּדֶּרֶךְ הִילּוּכוֹ מָצְאוּ אֶחָד הַהוֹלֵךְ מִמְּקוֹם הַבֵּית דִּין (עַל פִּי עֵרוּב, אוֹ בִּרְשׁוּת לְצֹרֶךְ), וְאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁכְּבָר קִדְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין עַל פִּי עֵדִים

And it appears to me: if along his way he encountered someone coming from the place of the court (by virtue of an eruv, or permissibly for a necessary purpose), who told him that the court already sanctified [the month] based on witnesses —
דְּאֶפְשָׁר דְּלֹא יְחַלֵּל שׁוּב לֵילֵךְ, אִם הוּא עֲדַיִן יוֹתֵר מִתְּחוּם;
that it is possible he should not continue to desecrate [Shabbat] to go further, if he is still beyond the boundary;
אֲבָל אִם אֵינוֹ יוֹתֵר מִתְּחוּם — וַדַּאי רַשַּׁאי, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּהִתְקִין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
but if he is not beyond the boundary — he is certainly permitted, as mentioned above, for Rabban Gamliel the Elder enacted that he may walk two thousand cubits.
וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן, דְּאֶפְשָׁר גַּם בָּזֶה חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא יִמָּנַע:
Yet this requires analysis, for it is possible that here too we are concerned lest he be deterred [in the future].
לֹא בָּאוּ עֵדִים — עוֹשִׂים חֹדֶשׁ מְעֻבָּר.
If witnesses did not arrive — they make the month intercalated [full, thirty days].
וּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מְקַבְּלִים עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כָּל הַיּוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים.
And originally, they would accept new-moon testimony all throughout the thirtieth day.
פַּעַם אַחַת נִשְׁתָּהוּ הָעֵדִים מִלָּבוֹא עַד בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, וְנִתְקַלְקְלוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְלֹא יָדְעוּ מַה יַּעֲשׂוּ:
Once, the witnesses were delayed in arriving until the late afternoon, and confusion occurred in the Temple, and they did not know what to do:
אִם יַעֲשׂוּ עוֹלָה שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם — שֶׁמָּא יָבוֹאוּ הָעֵדִים, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיַּקְרִיבוּ מוּסַף הַיּוֹם אַחַר תָּמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם
whether to offer the afternoon daily burnt-offering — lest witnesses arrive, and it is impossible to offer the day’s Musaf offering after the afternoon daily offering
(כֵּן מַשְׁמַע לְשׁוֹן הַבָּרַיְתָא (דַּף ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁהוּת לְהַקְרִיב" וְכוּלֵי
(so implies the language of the Baraita (folio 30b): "so that there will be time to offer," etc. —
מַשְׁמַע דְּחָשַׁשׁ מֵהַקְרָבָה, וְתָנָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי נָקַט;
meaning there was concern about the offering, and the Tanna of our Mishnah mentioned one of two things;
וְהָרַמְבַּ״ם בְּשִׁיר סָמַךְ עַל "וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם", שֶׁהַשִּׁיר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הוּא בִּכְלַל הַנְּסָכִים; כֵּן נִרְאֶה פָּשׁוּט.
and the Rambam, regarding the song of the Levites, relied upon "and their libations," for the song where required is categorized under libations; so it appears obvious.
וְעַיֵּן בְּלֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה וְתוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב.
And see Lechem Mishneh and Tosafot Yom Tov.
וְעַיֵּן בְּתוֹסָפוֹת, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וְנִתְקַלְקְלוּ", הִקְשׁוּ, וְכָתְבוּ: "וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר" וְכוּלֵי, "דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה דְּרַבִּים וְדָחֵי עֲשֵׂה דְּהַשְׁלָמָה" וְכוּלֵי.

And see Tosafot, s.v. "Venitkalkelu," who challenged this and wrote: "and one may say," etc., "that a communal positive commandment comes and overrides the positive commandment of completion [hashlamah]," etc.
וְלֹא הֵבַנְתִּי, דְּהָא אַחַר כָּךְ כָּתְבוּ "וְנִרְאֶה לִי דִּלְכַתְּחִלָּה" וְכוּלֵי;
Yet I do not understand, for afterwards they wrote: "and it appears to me that ab initio," etc.;
וּלְכַתְּחִלָּה וַדַּאי גַּם זֶה אָסוּר לְהָבִיא עַצְמוֹ אַף בְּדָחֵי בְּדִין, מִכָּל מָקוֹם דְּחוּיָה לֹא הוּתְּרָה.
and ab initio it is certainly forbidden to bring oneself into such a situation, for even where an override applies legally, an overridden prohibition is not wholly permitted.
וְגַם אֶפְשָׁר דְּזֶה מִקְרִי לַעֲשׂוֹת שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּשֶׁיִּתְקָנוּ, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּהָא אִתֶּם אֲפִלּוּ מְזִידִין.
And it is also possible that this is considered fulfilling both when properly enacted, as mentioned above, for "even if you act intentionally [the sanctification stands]".
וּבֶאֱמֶת מַשְׁמָעוּת הַבָּרַיְתָא כֵּן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וּמַתְנִיתִין חֲדָא נָקְטָא, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל — כֵּן הוּא פָּשׁוּט).
(And truly, the plain meaning of the Baraita is as mentioned above, and the Mishnah cited one detail as noted — so it is straightforward).
עָמְדוּ בֵּית דִּין וְהִתְקִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מְקַבְּלִים עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ אֶלָּא עַד זְמַן הַמִּנְחָה קְטַנָּה, שֶׁהוּא עַד תֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה שֶׁל הַיּוֹם
The court arose and enacted that they should not accept new-moon testimony except until the time of Minchah Ketanah, which is until nine and a half hours of the day
(סֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "הִתְקִינוּ"),
(Sefer Turei Even, s.v. "Hitkinu"),
כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא שָׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם לְהַקְרִיב מוּסָפִין, וְתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם, וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם.
so that there would be sufficient time during the day to offer the Musaf offerings, the afternoon daily offering, and their libations.
וְאִם הִגִּיעַ מִנְחָה וְלֹא בָּאוּ עֵדִים — עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם קֹדֶשׁ
And if Minchah arrived and witnesses had not come — they treat that day as holy
(לָא יָדְעִנָא — לְפִי מַה דְּאָמְרֵי בְּכָל חֳדָשִׁים, מַאי "קֹדֶשׁ"? וְאַכּוּלֵּי יוֹמָא קָאֵי. וְנִרְאֶה: דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר אַהֶסְפֵּד וְתַעֲנִית),
(I do not know: according to those who explain this across all months, what is "holy"? And it refers to the entire day! It seems: one may explain this regarding eulogy and fasting),
וּמַקְרִיבִין מוּסָף לְמָחָר, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ אַחַר מִנְחָה.
and they offer Musaf on the morrow, since they would not sanctify it after Minchah.
מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כָּל הַיּוֹם כֻּלּוֹ;
After the Temple was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai enacted that they should accept new-moon testimony the entire day;
וַאֲפִלּוּ בָּאוּ עֵדִים גַּם שְׁלוֹשִׁים סָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה — מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּתָן, וּמְקַדְּשִׁין יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים בִּלְבַד
and even if witnesses came on the thirtieth close to sunset — they accept their testimony and sanctify the thirtieth day alone

(וְזֶהוּ דַּעַת הָרַמְבַּ״ם; אֲבָל מִדִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י וְתוֹסָפוֹת וּשְׁאָר מְפָרְשִׁים מַשְׁמַע לְהֶדְיָא, דְּרַק בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הָיְתָה תַּקָּנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא לְקַבֵּל עֵדוּת מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה, מִשּׁוּם שִׁיר,

(and this is the opinion of the Rambam; however, from the words of Rashi, Tosafot, and other commentators it is explicitly implied that only on Rosh Hashanah was the first enactment made not to receive testimony from Minchah onward, due to the Levites' song,

and they observe that day as holy with respect to forbidden work — but not on other months.
וְעַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן, יִישֵּׁב עַל פִּי זֶה הָא דְּנָקַט שִׁיר וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם מוּסָף, עַיֵּן שָׁם):
(And see Sefer Turei Even, who reconciled based on this why the text specified song and not the Musaf offering, see there).
וּכְשֶׁמְּעַבְּרִין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ, כְּשֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ עֵדִים כָּל הַיּוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים
And when they intercalate the month, when witnesses did not come all throughout the thirtieth day —
הָיוּ עוֹלִין לְמָקוֹם מוּכָן, וְעוֹשִׂין בּוֹ סְעוּדָה בְּלֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד, שֶׁהוּא רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ.
they would ascend to a designated place and hold a festive meal on the night of the thirty-first, which is Rosh Chodesh.
וְאֵין עוֹלִין לְשָׁם בַּלַּיְלָה, אֶלָּא מִשְּׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה בְּיוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים, בְּעוֹד יוֹם קְצָת, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאוּם עוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים עוֹלִים; וְעִקַּר הַסְּעוּדָה תְּהֵא בַּלַּיְלָה.

And they do not ascend there at night, but from sunset on the thirtieth day, while there is still a little daylight, so that passersby on the roads see them ascending; and the primary meal was at night.
וְאֵין עוֹלִין לִסְעוּדָה זוֹ פָּחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם; וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּבָשָׂר וּשְׁאָר מַעֲדַנִּים, אֶלָּא בְּפַת דָּגָן וְקִטְנִית בִּלְבַד.
And they do not ascend to this meal fewer than ten men; nor do they ascend to it with meat and other delicacies, but only with grain bread and legumes.
וְזוֹ הִיא סְעוּדַת מִצְוָה, וְאֵינָהּ לֹא מִן הַתּוֹרָה, אֶלָּא תַּקָּנַת חֲכָמִים הָיְתָה לְפַרְסֵם הַדָּבָר
And this is a se'udat mitzvah, and it is not from the Torah, but was an enactment of the Sages to publicize the matter
(עַיֵּן תּוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב פֶּרֶק ח׳ דְּסַנְהֶדְרִין מִשְׁנָה ב׳, וּבְתוֹסָפוֹת חֲדָשִׁים).
((see Tosafot Yom Tov, Chapter 8 of Sanhedrin, Mishnah 2, and in Tosafot Chadashim).
וּכְשֶׁיּוֹרְדִים — יָרְדוּ בְּהַשְׁכָּמָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁהָרוֹאֶה אוֹתָם יוֹרְדִים יֵדַע שֶׁיָּשְׁבוּ שָׁם כָּל הַלַּיְלָה,
And when descending — they descended early in the morning, so that anyone seeing them descending would know that they sat there all night,
וְלֹא יַחְשׁוֹב שֶׁעַכְשָׁיו עָלוּ, וְיִתְפַּרְסֵם הַדָּבָר.
and not think they had only just ascended, so that the matter would be publicized.
כָּל זֶה לְפֵרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י בַּגְּמָרָא, פֶּרֶק בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה (דַּף ע׳ עַמּוּד ב׳).
(All this is according to Rashi’s explanation in the Gemara, Chapter "Ben Sorer U'Moreh" (folio 70b).
אֲבָל הָרַמְבַּ״ם כָּתַב: "וְאֵין עוֹלִין בַּלַּיְלָה, אֶלָּא בַּנֶּשֶׁף, קֹדֶם עֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר" (נִרְאֶה דְּצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר "הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ").
However, the Rambam wrote: "And they do not ascend at night, but in the twilight, before the rise of dawn" (it seems it should read "the sun").
נִרְאֶה דִּמְפָרֵשׁ "אַחְרִיפוּ" הַיְנוּ קֹדֶם עֲלוֹת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, בְּסוֹף הַלַּיְלָה — לֹא בִּתְחִלַּת הַלַּיְלָה.
It appears he explains "achrifu" as before sunrise, at the end of the night — not at the beginning of the night.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין אֵיךְ מְיַשֵּׁב הַקֻּשְׁיָא בָּזֶה.
And one needs to understand how he resolves the difficulty in this.
וְאוּלַי דְּרוֹצֶה לוֹמַר: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא יוֹם וְלֹא לַיְלָה, דְּגַם בְּשַׁחֲרִית יֵשׁ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, כַּיָּדוּעַ;
And perhaps he means to say: at a time that is neither day nor night, for in the morning there is also a twilight period, as is known;
וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן "נֶשֶׁף", כִּדְאִיתָא (פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת): "נְשַׁף לֵילְיָא וְאָתֵי יְמָמָא".
and this is the terminology of "neshef," as found in the first chapter of Berakhot: "the night expired and the day came."
וְלָכֵן אָמַר פַּעַם אַחַת "בַּיּוֹם", וְלֹא "בַּלַּיְלָה", וּפַעַם אַחַת "בַּלַּיְלָה" וְלֹא "בַּיּוֹם";
And therefore it stated once "by day" and not "by night," and once "by night" and not "by day";

וְכַהַאי גַּוְנָא (פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּשַׁבָּת) בְּכַרְמְלִית — מַאי טַעְמָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ "רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים"? לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד; מַאי טַעְמָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ "רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד"? לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים.

similar to the first chapter of Shabbat regarding a karmelit: Why is it called a public domain? Because it is not a private domain; why is it called a private domain? Because it is not a public domain.

And it appears that he was compelled to explain thus to resolve the question of Tosafot, s.v. "Ve'ein," etc.;
דִּלְפִי זֶה נִיחָא, דִּלְאוֹר עִבּוּרוֹ לְמַעֵט יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים, וְאַלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה לְמַעֵט יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד.
for according to this it works out well, that "by the light of its intercalation" excludes the thirtieth day, and "only at night" excludes the thirty-first day.

Nonetheless, Rashi's opinion seems primary in the language of the Gemara;
וְגַם לְדַעַת רַשִׁ״י יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ כֵּן — אֵין עוֹלִין בְּיוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה.
and even according to Rashi one can explain thus — they do not ascend on the thirty-first day, but at night.
וְעוֹד דְּקָשֶׁה לְהָרַמְבַּ״ם: אֵיךְ יֹאכַל אָז קֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה? וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
Furthermore, it is difficult according to the Rambam: how could one eat then prior to prayer? See there in its place.
גַּם לֹא יָדַעְתִּי לָמָּה הִשְׁמִיט הָרַמְבַּ״ם "אַחְרִיפוּ" וּ"פוּקוּ" — לְהַשְׁכִּים לָצֵאת; גַּם לֹא יָדַעְתִּי אֵיךְ מְפָרֵשׁ לָהּ, וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן:
I also do not know why the Rambam omitted "achrifu" and "fuku" — to rise early to leave; nor do I know how he interprets it, and it requires analysis.
אַחַר שֶׁקִּדְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין הַחֹדֶשׁ (וְכֵן עִבּוּר הַשָּׁנָה) — מִצְוָה לָהֶם לְהוֹדִיעַ לָעָם,
After the court sanctified the month (and likewise the intercalation of the year) — it is a mitzvah upon them to inform the people,
כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ אֲמִתַּת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ, וְיֵדְעוּ הַמּוֹעֲדוֹת אֵיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת
so that they will know the true day of Rosh Chodesh, and know how to observe the festivals
(וְגַם בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ עַצְמוֹ נַפְקָא מִינָּהּ לֶאֱסוֹר בְּהֶסְפֵּד וְתַעֲנִית, וַעֲשִׂיַּת מְלָאכָה לְנָשִׁים).
((and on Rosh Chodesh itself there is also practical relevance to prohibit eulogies and fasting, and work for women).
וּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַשִּׂיאִין מַשּׂוּאוֹת בְּכָל חֹדֶשׁ (כֵּן כָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "הָיוּ"):
And originally they would light flares for every month (so it is written in Sefer Turei Even, s.v. "Hayu"):
כְּשֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה בִּזְמַנּוֹ, לְקַדְּשׁוֹ בְּיוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים — הָיוּ מַשִּׂיאִין בַּלַּיְלָה שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו, לֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד;
when it was seen in its proper time, to sanctify it on the thirtieth day — they would light flares on the following night, the eve of the thirty-first;
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהָיָה מְעֻבָּר — לֹא הָיוּ מַשִּׂיאִין כְּלָל, וְהָיוּ הַכֹּל יוֹדְעִים: כְּשֶׁלֹּא הִשִּׂיאוּ — שֶׁהוּא מְעֻבָּר, וּכְשֶׁהִשִּׂיאוּ — שֶׁנִּרְאָה בִּזְמַנּוֹ.

but when it was intercalated [thirty days] — they would not light flares at all, and everyone knew: when they did not light flares — that it was intercalated, and when they lit flares — that it had been seen in its time.
וְאִם חָל יוֹם שְׁלוֹשִׁים בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַשִּׂיא בְּלֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד, שֶׁהוּא בְּשַׁבָּת
And if the thirtieth day fell on the eve of Shabbat, making it impossible to light flares on the eve of the thirty-first which is Shabbat —
מַשִּׂיאִין בְּלֵיל שְׁלוֹשִׁים וּשְׁנַיִם, בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת;
they would light flares on the eve of the thirty-second, on Saturday night;
וְהַכֹּל יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהָיָה חָסֵר, שֶׁהֲרֵי אִם לָאו — אֵין מַשִּׂיאִים
and everyone knew that it had been deficient [twenty-nine days], for if not — flares would not be lit at all
(וּבְעִבּוּר שָׁנָה, עַיֵּן בְּטוּרֵי אֶבֶן, שֶׁכָּתַב: אֶפְשָׁר גַּם אָז הָיוּ שְׁלוּחִין יוֹצְאִים עַל זֶה, אוֹ הָיוּ מַשִּׂיאִים אֵיזֶה יָמִים בַּחֹדֶשׁ לְהוֹדִיעַ שֶׁהוּא אֲדָר שֵׁנִי).
((and regarding the leap year, see Turei Even, who wrote: perhaps even then messengers went out for this, or they lit flares on certain days of the month to announce that it was Adar Sheni).
וְאֵין מַשִּׂיאִים אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה, דִּבַיּוֹם — "שְׁרַגָּא בְּטִיהֲרָא מַאי מְהַנֵּי":
And they light flares only at night, for during the day — "what benefit is a candle at noon?"
וְעַל כִּסְלֵו — מִפְּנֵי חֲנֻכָּה.
And for Kislev — on account of Chanukah.
וּפָשׁוּט דְּיֵלְכוּ עַד סוֹפָהּ שֶׁל חֲנֻכָּה.
And it is obvious that they would go until the end of Chanukah.
(וְעַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן (דַּף י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳), דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּם", לִדְבָרָיו שָׁם דִּבַּחֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים יַחְמִירוּ מִסָּפֵק, עַיֵּן שָׁם הֵיטֵב;

(And see in Sefer Turei Even (folio 18b), s.v. "Bizman SheBeit HaMikdash Kayam," according to his words there that regarding Chanukah and Purim they would be stringent out of doubt, examine well there;
אִם כֵּן, אִם קִדְּשׁוּ בִּזְמַנּוֹ — צָרִיךְ לֵילֵךְ עַד לֵיל תְּשִׁיעִי דַּחֲנֻכָּה, וְיוֹמוֹ,
if so, if they sanctified it in its proper time — they would need to go until the ninth night of Chanukah, and its day,

And see in Sefer Turei Even, where he challenged Tosafot at length and cited the words of the Ba'al HaMa'or [Razah], who explained along a different path, and according to their words there is no full proof.

since he held like Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Tzadok that only on the thirtieth day does one say "It is sanctified," but not on the thirty-first;

Perhaps for the amount of time in which they could have sanctified it, on account of a decree, as mentioned above; or alternatively until the intercalation meal; and this requires study.

וּבַמְּקוֹמוֹת הָרְחוֹקִים, שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁלוּחִים מַגִּיעִים אֲלֵיהֶם — הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים שְׁנֵי יָמִים, מִפְּנֵי הַסָּפֵק,
And in distant places where the messengers did not reach them — they would observe two days, out of doubt,
לְפִי שֶׁאֵין יוֹדְעִים יוֹם שֶׁקָּבְעוּ בֵּית דִּין הַחֹדֶשׁ אֵיזֶהוּ — אִם שְׁלוֹשִׁים אוֹ שְׁלוֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד.
because they did not know which day the court established the new month — whether the thirtieth or the thirty-first.
כָּךְ הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין בְּכָל יוֹם טוֹב;
Thus would they do on every festival;
אֲבָל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד,
but Yom Kippur they observed for only one day,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא סַכָּנָה לְהִתְעַנּוֹת שְׁנֵי יָמִים בְּבַת אַחַת וּלְהַפְסִיק מִקֹּדֶם;
because it is dangerous to fast two consecutive days without pause;
וּלְפִיכָךְ סָמְכוּ עַל הַחֲזָקָה שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִים מִלְּקַדֵּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ.
and therefore they relied on the presumption that the court is not negligent in sanctifying the month in its proper time.
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל פֵּרוּשׁוֹ;
(Jerusalem Talmud, as I wrote above in its explanation;

וְעַיֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל בְּדִבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י דִּפְסָחִים, שֶׁבְּאֵלוּל שֶׁחָל בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, דַּלֶּת, אוֹ וָו הֲוֵי סָפֵק, וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ חֲזָקָה זוֹ, וְצָרִיךְ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שְׁנֵי יָמִים.)
(and see what I wrote above regarding Rashi in Pesachim, that on days of doubt when it falls on Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday this presumption does not apply, requiring two days for Yom Kippur).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲשֶׂה הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּים יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שְׁנֵי יָמִים, מִסְּפֵיקָא דְּיוֹמָא (דַּף כ״א עַמּוּד א׳: "רָבָא" וְכוּלֵי, וּבִירוּשַׁלְמִי):
(Nonetheless, there were scrupulous individuals who fasted Yom Kippur for two days, out of the calendar doubt (folio 21a: "Rava," etc., and in the Jerusalem Talmud).
וּבַחֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים — נִרְאֶה לִי פָּשׁוּט, בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁלוּחִים מַגִּיעִים לֹא יַעֲשׂוּ אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד, דְּמִדְּרַבָּנָן הוּא, וּסְפֵיקוֹ לְהָקֵל;

And regarding Chanukah and Purim — it seems obvious to me that in places where the messengers do not reach they observe only one day, for it is rabbinic, and a doubt in rabbinic law is judged leniently;
וְתֵדַע, דְּלֹא עָבְדִינַן הָאִידָּנָא מִסְּפֵיקָא דְּיוֹמָא בַּחֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים.
and know this to be true, for nowadays we do not practice two days out of doubt on Chanukah and Purim.

וְעַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן (דַּף י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳), דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּם" — לֹא כָּתַב כֵּן, וְטַעְמוֹ: דְּלֹא שַׁיָּךְ סְפֵיקָא דְּרַבָּנָן לְהָקֵל, דְּיִתְבַּטֵּל כָּל הַדְּרַבָּנָן, עַיֵּן שָׁם בַּאֲרִיכוּת.

And see in Sefer Turei Even (folio 18b) s.v. "Bizman SheBeit HaMikdash Kayam" — he did not write thus, his rationale being that leniency in rabbinic doubt does not apply where it would abolish the entire rabbinic enactment, see there at length.
וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: בַּחֲנֻכָּה פָּשׁוּט, דְּלֹא יִתְבַּטֵּל כְּלָל כָּל הַדְּרַבָּנָן אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֵין זֶה קָרוּי בִּטּוּל כָּל הַדְּרַבָּנָן.

And I say: regarding Chanukah it is obvious, for the entire rabbinic enactment would not be uprooted at all, only a single day, and that is not termed the abolition of the entire rabbinic institution.
מִיהוּ, בְּלָאו הָכֵי לֹא קָשֶׁה מִידֵּי בֵּין בַּחֲנֻכָּה בֵּין בְּפוּרִים
However, even without this it presents no difficulty either on Chanukah or on Purim —
דְּאַטּוּ בְּנֵי בָבֶל לֹא קָבְעוּ שׁוּם קְבִיעוּת עַד שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל? זֶה אֵין הַדַּעַת סוֹבַלְתּוֹ.
for did the people of Babylonia establish no calendar until they heard from the Land of Israel? Reason cannot tolerate this.
וְעַיֵּן (בְּדַף כ״א רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳) וּבַתּוֹסָפוֹת, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "לֵוִי" — נַמִּי לֹא מַשְׁמַע כֵּן;
And see (folio 21a) and Tosafot s.v. "Levi" — which likewise does not indicate this;
אֶלָּא בְּנֵי בָבֶל הָיוּ קוֹבְעִין לָהֶם כְּפִי רְאוּת עֵינֵיהֶם, וּמוֹנִים לָהֶם; אֲבָל לֹא לְעִקָּר, עַד שֶׁיּוֹדִיעוּ לָהֶם מִבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
rather, the people of Babylonia established the calendar according to their own assessment and counted accordingly, though not as definitive until informed by the court of the Land of Israel.
וְאִם כֵּן, וַדַּאי קָבְעוּ גַּם חֲנֻכָּה וּפוּרִים לְפִי קְבִיעָתָם, וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ דְּמִסָּפֵק יִתְבַּטֵּל הַכֹּל — דְּהָא לֹא יִתְבַּטֵּל, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
If so, they certainly observed Chanukah and Purim according to their calculation, and there is no concern that out of doubt the entire observance would be lost — for it was not lost, as noted;
וְעַיֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל עַל דִּבְרֵי הַטּוּרֵי אֶבֶן.
and see what I wrote above on the words of the Turei Even.
וּקְצָת רְאָיָה לְמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי מִדִּבְרֵי רַשִׁ״י (דַּף כ״ג עַמּוּד א׳), דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "אָמַר אַבָּיֵי", שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ אַרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה;
And partial proof for what I wrote emerges from Rashi (folio 23a) s.v. "Amar Abaye," who explained it regarding Rosh Hashanah;
וְעַיֵּן שָׁם בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מִשּׁוּם" וְכוּלֵי, וּלְחִנָּם דָּחֲקוּ וְכוּלֵי בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
and see Tosafot there s.v. "Mishum," etc., who struggled needlessly regarding Rosh Chodesh, see there.
וּלְמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי — יֵשׁ לוֹמַר: דַּהֲלֹא רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ דְּרַבָּנָן, וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ מִסָּפֵק יַחְמִיר;
And according to what I wrote — one can say: Rosh Chodesh is rabbinic, so being stringent out of doubt does not apply;
וְגַם אַוַּדַּאי לְתַקֵּן — זֶה אֵין לְהִזָּקֵק, כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ חִיּוּבָא בֶּאֱמֶת, אֶלָּא מִנְהָגָא;
and furthermore, establishing an enactment for certainty is uncalled for, as it is truly custom rather than absolute obligation;
וְרַק לְהַצִּילָם מִבִּטּוּל מְלָאכָה הֻצְרְכוּ; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה. עַיֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל עַל דִּבְרֵיהֶם, לְיַשֵּׁב קֻשְׁיַת טוּרֵי אֶבֶן:
(and they only needed to save them from unnecessary cessation of work; unlike Rosh Hashanah. See what I wrote above to reconcile the difficulty of the Turei Even).
וּבִמְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ מַגִּיעִים אֲלֵיהֶם שְׁלוּחֵי נִיסָן, וְלֹא הִגִּיעוּ שְׁלוּחֵי תִּשְׁרֵי
And in places that the messengers of Nisan reached, but the messengers of Tishrei did not reach —
וּמִן הַדִּין הָיָה שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ פֶּסַח יוֹם אֶחָד, שֶׁהֲרֵי הִגִּיעוּ לָהֶם שְׁלוּחִין וְיָדְעוּ בְּאֵיזֶה יוֹם נִקְבַּע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ;
and by strict law they ought to have observed Pesach for one day, since the messengers reached them and they knew on which day Rosh Chodesh was established;
וְיַעֲשׂוּ יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל סֻכּוֹת שְׁנֵי יָמִים, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא הִגִּיעוּ לָהֶם הַשְּׁלוּחִין
and they would observe the festival of Sukkot for two days, since the messengers did not reach them —
וּכְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לַחֲלוֹק בַּמּוֹעֲדוֹת, הִתְקִינוּ חֲכָמִים שֶׁכָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין שְׁלוּחֵי תִּשְׁרֵי מַגִּיעִין — שָׁם עוֹשִׂין שְׁנֵי יָמִים (גְּזֵרָה נִיסָן אַטּוּ תִּשְׁרֵי).

(in order not to create disparity among the festivals, the Sages enacted that wherever the messengers of Tishrei do not reach — they observe two days everywhere (a decree on Nisan on account of Tishrei).
וְנִרְאֶה דְּאַטּוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֹא בָּעוּ לְמִגְזַר — דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָאו בִּכְלַל שְׁלוֹשָׁה יָמִים טוֹבִים נִינְהוּ.
And it appears they did not decree on account of Rosh Hashanah — because Rosh Hashanah is not categorized within the Three Pilgrimage Festivals.
וְעַיֵּן בְּסֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן, הֶאֱרִיךְ — וַאֲפִלּוּ יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת:
(And see in Sefer Turei Even, who elaborated — that this applied even to the festival of Shavuot).
וְכַמָּה בֵּין שְׁלוּחֵי נִיסָן לִשְׁלוּחֵי תִּשְׁרֵי? שְׁנֵי יָמִים:
And what is the difference between the messengers of Nisan and those of Tishrei? Two days:
שֶׁשְּׁלוּחֵי תִּשְׁרֵי אֵין מְהַלְּכִין בְּאֶחָד בְּתִשְׁרֵי, שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב, וְלֹא בַּעֲשָׂרָה בּוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וּשְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת — הֲרֵי עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים;
for the messengers of Tishrei do not travel on the first of Tishrei, which is a festival, nor on the tenth, which is Yom Kippur, plus two Sabbaths — leaving ten travel days;
וּבְנִיסָן דַּל שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת — פָּשׁ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יָמִים.
whereas in Nisan, subtract only two Sabbaths — leaving twelve travel days.
וַאֲפִלּוּ הָיְתָה שָׁנָה שֶׁרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אוֹ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁלָּהּ בְּשַׁבָּת, וְיֵשׁ אַחַד עָשָׂר יָמִים, וְגַם שְׁלוּחֵי תִּשְׁרֵי מַגִּיעִין לוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ שָׁנָה
And even in a year where Rosh Hashanah or Yom Kippur fell on Shabbat, yielding eleven travel days where messengers of Tishrei could reach that place in that year —
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא תִּשְׁרֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הֶפְסֵק אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים, גּוֹזְרִין כָּל נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי אַטּוּ תִּשְׁרֵי זֶה
nevertheless, since there are years where Tishrei has an interruption of four non-travel days, they decreed for all instances of Nisan and Tishrei on account of such a Tishrei
(סֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן דַּף כ׳ עַמּוּד ב׳, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "גְּזֵרָה").
(Sefer Turei Even folio 20b, s.v. "Gezerah").
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לָהֶם לַשְּׁלוּחִים לֵילֵךְ אַף בְּנִיסָן עַד הֶחָג;
Nonetheless, the messengers must continue walking even in Nisan until the festival;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יוֹעִיל לִשְׁנוֹת לְעִנְיַן יוֹם טוֹב — מִכָּל מָקוֹם יְהֵא נַפְקָא מִינָּהּ לְעִנְיַן מֵת, וְכַהַאי גַּוְנָא
even though it will not alter the two-day observance of the festival — there is still practical halakhic relevance for burial of the dead on the second day, and the like
(סֵפֶר טוּרֵי אֶבֶן שָׁם, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "כָּל").
(Sefer Turei Even ibid., s.v. "Kol").
וְאֵין הַשְּׁלוּחִים צְרִיכִים שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנַיִם, אֶלָּא אֲפִלּוּ אֶחָד נֶאֱמָן;
And the messengers need not be two, for even a single individual is believed;
וְלֹא שָׁלִיחַ בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא אֲפִלּוּ תַּגָּר מִשְּׁאָר הָעָם שֶׁבָּא כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וְאוֹמֵר: "אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁקִּדְּשׁוּ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי" — נֶאֱמָן

and not an appointed messenger alone, but even an ordinary merchant traveling casually who says: "I heard from the mouth of the court that they sanctified the month on such-and-such day" — is believed
(נִרְאֶה דְּנַפְקָא לֵיהּ מִגְּמָרָא (דַּף כ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) — וְגִירְסָתוֹ "אֶחָד מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם", וְכֵן הוּא בְּלֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה.
(it seems he derives this from the Gemara (folio 22b) — reading "one from the end of the world," as found in Lechem Mishneh.

for even if the court intercalated willfully against the law — the intercalation stands, as will be explained below;

However, they intimidate them with great admonition, pressuring them with probing questions and detailed cross-examinations, scrutinizing the testimony,

and the court strives not to sanctify this month, since its status as an intercalated month was already publicized.

they sanctify it, and count that month from the thirtieth day, since the moon appeared on its night.

And if the court needs to leave this month intercalated as it was — they leave it.

(and he did not strictly formulate "to leave," but since he presented the laws in sequence, he wrote thus; see what I wrote above, and it is obvious).

And this is what the Sages stated: They intercalate the month for a communal need.
וְיֵשׁ מִן הַחֲכָמִים הַגְּדוֹלִים מִי שֶׁחוֹלֵק בָּזֶה, וְאוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ לְצֹרֶךְ;
Yet there is one among the great Sages who disagrees, asserting: They never intercalate the month for a communal need;
הוֹאִיל וּבָאוּ עֵדִים — מְקַדְּשִׁין, וְאֵין מְאַיְּמִין עֲלֵיהֶם.
since witnesses arrived — they sanctify it, and do not intimidate them.

And the dispute among the Sages is only regarding other months, excluding Nisan and Tishrei;
אוֹ בְּעֵדֵי נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי שֶׁבָּאוּ אַחַר שֶׁעָבְרוּ הָרְגָלִים, שֶׁכְּבָר נַעֲשָׂה מַה שֶּׁנַּעֲשָׂה, וְעָבַר זְמַן הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת וְהַמּוֹעֲדוֹת.
or regarding witnesses for Nisan and Tishrei who arrived after the festivals passed, where what was done is done, and the time for sacrifices and festivals has elapsed.
אֲבָל אִם בָּאוּ הָעֵדִים בְּנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי קֹדֶם חֲצִי הַחֹדֶשׁ — מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּתָן, וְאֵין מְאַיְּמִין עֲלֵיהֶם כְּלָל;
However, if the witnesses for Nisan and Tishrei arrived before the middle of the month — they accept their testimony, and do not intimidate them at all;
שֶׁאֵין מְאַיְּמִין עַל עֵדִים שֶׁהֵעִידוּ עַל הַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁרָאוּהוּ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, כְּדֵי לְעַבְּרוֹ.
for they never intimidate witnesses who testified that they saw the new moon in its time in order to intercalate it.
אֲבָל מְאַיְּמִין עַל עֵדִים שֶׁנִּתְקַלְקְלָה עֵדוּתָן
However, they do intimidate witnesses whose testimony became confused or flawed —
וַהֲרֵי הַדָּבָר גְּנַאי שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְקַיֵּם הָעֵדוּת, וְיִתְעַבֵּר הַחֹדֶשׁ
and it is considered a disgrace for the testimony to collapse causing the month to be intercalated [improperly] —
מְאַיְּמִין עֲלֵיהֶן, כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְקַיֵּם הָעֵדוּת, וְיִתְקַיֵּם הַחֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ.
they intimidate them so that the testimony is verified and the month is established in its proper time.
וְכֵן אִם בָּאוּ הָעֵדִים לְהָזִים אֶת הָעֵדִים שֶׁרָאוּהוּ בִּזְמַנּוֹ, קֹדֶם שֶׁיְּקַדְּשׁוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין
And likewise, if witnesses came to refute [hazamah] the witnesses who saw it in its proper time, prior to the court's sanctification —
הֲרֵי אָנוּ מְאַיְּמִין עַל הַמְּזִימִין, עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְקַיֵּם הַהֲזָמָה, וְיִתְקַדֵּשׁ הַחֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ
behold, we intimidate the refuting witnesses so that the refutation does not stand, and the month is sanctified in its proper time
(מַשְׁמַע דִּבְזֶה אֵין מַחְלֹקֶת, וְהַכֹּל מוֹדִים).
((implying that in this matter there is no dispute, and all agree).
וְהוּא הַדִּין: שֶׁאִם רָאוּ צֹרֶךְ בַּדָּבָר, וְהֻצְרְכוּ בֵּית דִּין לְהַנִּיחַ אוֹתוֹ חֹדֶשׁ מְקֻדָּשׁ — מַנִּיחִין, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל בִּמְעֻבָּר:
(And the same applies: if the court saw a communal need and had to keep that month sanctified [deficient] — they keep it so, as mentioned above regarding intercalating).
וְהִנֵּה כָּל זֶה — דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם [רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן].
Now all this — reflects the words of the Rambam.
וְנִרְאֶה לִי דְּנַפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהַגְּמָרָא (דַּף כ׳ עַמּוּד א׳):
And it appears to me that he derived it from the Gemara (folio 20a):
"אִינִי? וְהָתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל" וְכוּלֵי
"Is that so? But didn't Rabba bar Shmuel teach," etc. —
"לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לְעַבְּרוֹ, כָּאן לְקַדְּשׁוֹ" וְכוּלֵי;
"This is not difficult: here [it refers] to intercalating it, there to sanctifying it," etc.;
"וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מְאַיְּמִין" וְכוּלֵי.
"and like that which Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: They intimidate," etc.
וְהִנֵּה, מֵהָא דְּקָאָמַר "וְכִי הָא" וְכוּלֵי — מַשְׁמַע דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִלְּתָא אַחֲרִיתָא קָאָמַר.
And behold, from the fact that it says "and like that," etc. — it implies that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was stating a distinct matter.
וְעוֹד, דְּאִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי נַמִּי מִלְּצֹרֶךְ — אִם כֵּן, אַדְּרַבָּא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי פָּלִיג עַל זֶה;
Furthermore, if Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi also referred to a communal need — if so, on the contrary, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disputes this;
דְּמִתְּחִלָּה קָאָמַר מְעַבְּרִין לְצֹרֶךְ, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְאַיֵּם כְּלָל;
for initially it stated that they intercalate for a need, requiring no intimidation at all;
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי קָאָמַר: "מְאַיְּמִין" — הָא אִם אִיְּמוּ וְלֹא הוֹעִיל, מַשְׁמַע דְּאֵין מְעַבְּרִים;
whereas Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi stated: "They intimidate" — which implies that if they intimidated and it was ineffective, they do not intercalate;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם [רַבֵּינוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן].
and as the Rambam wrote.
לְכָךְ מְפָרֵשׁ הָרַמְבַּ״ם דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִלְּתָא אַחֲרִיתָא קָאָמַר,
Therefore the Rambam explains that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was addressing a different scenario,
וְלָאו אַלְּצֹרֶךְ קָאֵי, אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁכְּבָר עִבְּרוּ אוֹ כְּבָר קִדְּשׁוּ.
and it does not refer to a communal need, but rather to a case where they had already intercalated or already sanctified.
וּמַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ לְהָרַמְבַּ״ם עוֹד הָכֵי, מִדְּקָאָמַר "עֵדִים" בְּלְקַדְּשׁוֹ;
And it is further implied to the Rambam in this manner from the mention of "witnesses" regarding sanctifying it;
וְאִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה לְקַדְּשׁוֹ לְצֹרֶךְ קָאָמַר — "עֵדִים" מַאן דְּכַר שְׁמַיְיהוּ?
for if it meant sanctifying it ab initio for a communal need — who mentioned witnesses at all?
וְאֵיזֶה עֵדִים נִתְפּוֹס לְאַיֵּם עֲלֵיהֶם?
And which witnesses would we seize to intimidate?
הֲלֹא כָּל הָעָם לֹא רָאוּ, וְעַל לֹא רָאוּ — אֵיךְ שַׁיָּךְ עֵדִים, וְעַל מִי נְאַיֵּם?
Behold, the entire populace did not see it, and regarding not seeing — how are witnesses relevant, and whom would we intimidate?
לְכָךְ מְפָרֵשׁ דְּמַיְירֵי [דְּמַיְירֵינַן] כְּשֶׁכְּבָר הֵעִידוּ עֵדִים, וּנְאַיֵּם עֲלֵיהֶם לְהַחֲזִיק עֵדוּתָן, וְשֶׁלֹּא יְזוֹמוּם; וּבָזֶה רַק מְאַיְּמִין.

Therefore he explains that it deals with a case where witnesses had already testified, and we intimidate them to uphold their testimony so that others do not refute them; and in this case they merely intimidate.
אֲבָל אִם אִיְּמוּ וְלֹא הוֹעִיל — חוֹזְרִין וּמוֹנִין כָּרָאוּי, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
However, if they intimidated and it was ineffective — they revert and reckon as appropriate, as mentioned above.
וּמְדַמֵּי לָהּ גְּמָרָא לְעִבּוּר לְצֹרֶךְ, שֶׁלֹּא בְּאִיּוּם;
And the Gemara compares it to intercalating for a need, which is done without intimidation;
וּכְמוֹ דְּמַפְלִיג רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי כָּאן בֵּין קִדּוּשׁ לְעִבּוּר — הָכֵי נַמִּי שָׁם:
and just as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi distinguishes here between sanctification and intercalation — so too does it apply there.
וְהִנֵּה בַּסּוֹף אַסֵּיק: רָבָא אָמַר — הָא דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל, אֲחֵרִים הוּא, וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
And behold, at the conclusion it finalized: Rava said — that which Rabba bar Shmuel taught represents the view of Acherim, etc., see there.
וְרָבָא בָּא לְיַשֵּׁב דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה אַחַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל;
And Rava came to reconcile the words of Rabbi Yehudah Nesi'ah following Rabba bar Shmuel;
אָתֵי דְּעוּלָּא — כְּבָר יִשֵּׁב רָבָא בְּעַצְמוֹ לְעֵיל: כָּאן לְקַדְּשׁוֹ, כָּאן לְעַבְּרוֹ.
as for Ulla's teaching — Rava himself already reconciled it above: here regarding sanctifying it, there regarding intercalating it.
וּלְרָבָא, אִם כֵּן לְדִידָן — דְּלָא קַיְימָא לַן כַּאֲחֵרִים — בֵּין מְעַבְּרִין בֵּין מְקַדְּשִׁין לְצֹרֶךְ;
And according to Rava, if so for us — since we do not hold like Acherim — we both intercalate and sanctify for a communal need;
וְהוּא הַדִּין לְאַיֵּם — דְּדָמֵי לִלְצֹרֶךְ, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
and the same applies to intimidating — which is similar to a communal need, as mentioned above;
וּכְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה, דְּגַם לְקַדֵּשׁ מְאַיְּמִין, וְלֵית לֵיהּ תֵּרוּץ אַבָּיֵי.
and in accord with the words of Rabbi Yehudah Nesi'ah, that they intimidate to sanctify as well, and he does not accept Abaye's resolution.
וְקַיְימָא לַן אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא — הֲלָכָה כְּרָבָא;
And we hold that between Abaye and Rava — the Halakhah follows Rava;
אִם כֵּן הֲלָכָה כְּרָבָא, דִּמְאַיְּמִין וְכֵן לְצֹרֶךְ עָבְדִינַן בְּכָל עִנְיָן, בֵּין לְקַדְּשׁוֹ בֵּין לְעַבְּרוֹ.
if so, the Halakhah follows Rava, that we intimidate and likewise act for a need in every situation, whether to sanctify it or to intercalate it.
אַךְ הִנֵּה בַּגְּמָרָא: אָמַר בָּתַר הָכֵי רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא: מַתְנֵי אִיפְּכָא וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
Yet behold, in the Gemara: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a stated after this: Reverse the teaching, etc., see there.
וְהִנֵּה, לְדִבְרֵי רַב דִּימִי אַתְיָין: תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל, וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה — עַל נָכוֹן;
And behold, according to the words of Rav Dimi, the teaching of Rabba bar Shmuel, the words of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and the words of Rabbi Yehudah Nesi'ah — align properly;
וּפְלִיגֵי אַדְּעוּלָּא, וְאֵין מְאַיְּמִין, וּלְצֹרֶךְ אֶלָּא לְקַדְּשׁוֹ — לֹא לְעַבְּרוֹ;
and they dispute Ulla, holding that they do not intimidate or act for a need except to sanctify it — but not to intercalate it;
וּלְדִידֵיהּ וַדַּאי כֵּן עִבְּרוּהוּ.
and according to him, they certainly intercalated it thus.
וְזֶהוּ "יֵשׁ מֵהַחֲכָמִים הַגְּדוֹלִים" וְכוּלֵי — וְהוּא רַב דִּימִי הַנִּזְכָּר.
And this is what was meant by "there is one among the great Sages," etc. — referring to the aforementioned Rav Dimi.
וּבִלְקַדְּשׁוֹ — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מוֹדוּ דִּמְאַיְּמִין, וְכֵן לְצֹרֶךְ, דִּכְהָדָדֵי נִינְהוּ, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
And regarding sanctifying it — everyone concedes that they intimidate and act for a need, since they are parallel, as mentioned above;
כִּי פְּלִיגֵי — בִּלְעַבְּרוֹ לְאִיּוּם וּלְצֹרֶךְ.
where they dispute — is regarding intercalating it through intimidation and for a need.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב דִּבְנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מוֹדוּ — הִנֵּה זֶה כָּתַב בְּ"יֵרָאֶה לִי" וְכוּלֵי;
And what is written that regarding Nisan and Tishrei everyone agrees — behold, this he wrote with the qualification "it appears to me," etc.;
וְהָרַמְבַּ״ם מִדְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ קָאָמַר לָהּ.
and the Rambam stated it from his own reasoned analysis.
וְהִנֵּה בַּגְּמָרָא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי כַּהַאי גַּוְנָא לְעִנְיַן לְקַדְּשׁוֹ, לְהַיֵּשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים שֶׁבַּתּוֹסָפוֹת, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "הָא";
And behold, in the Gemara Abaye stated a similar distinction regarding sanctifying it, according to some interpreters in Tosafot s.v. "Ha";
אַךְ לְפֵרוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י [רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי] הוּא אַדְּרַבָּא לְהֵפֶךְ.
yet according to Rashi's commentary it is, on the contrary, the exact opposite.
אֲבָל בְּלָאו הָכֵי — הָא רָבָא לֵית לֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי.
However, even aside from this — Rava does not accept Abaye's approach.
אַךְ הִנֵּה רָאִיתִי בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג׳ הֲלָכָה א׳):
Yet behold, I saw in the Jerusalem Talmud (beginning of Chapter 3, Halakhah 1):
אִיתָא — רַבִּי זְעִירָא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מְעַמְעֲמִין (פֵּרוּשׁ: מְאַיְּמִין) עַל הַנִּרְאֶה לְעַבְּרוֹ, וְלֹא עַל שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאֶה לְקַדְּשׁוֹ;
it is stated — Rabbi Ze'ira in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: They obscure/intimidate regarding that which is seen to intercalate it, but not regarding that which is not seen to sanctify it;
רַבִּי בָּא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מְעַמְעֲמִין עַל שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאֶה לְקַדְּשׁוֹ, וְלֹא עַל הַנִּרְאֶה לְעַבְּרוֹ, וְכוּלֵי;
Rabbi Ba in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: They intimidate regarding that which is not seen to sanctify it, but not regarding that which is seen to intercalate it, etc.;
וְלָא פְּלִיגִין — מַה דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זְעִירָא בִּשְׁאָר כָּל הַחֳדָשִׁים, מַה דְּאָמַר רַבִּי בָּא בְּנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי, עַד כָּאן:
and they do not dispute — what Rabbi Ze'ira said applies to all other months, while what Rabbi Ba said applies to Nisan and Tishrei; thus far.
וְלָמַדְנוּ מֵהַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי, דִּבְנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי מְאַיְּמִין לְקַדֵּשׁ וְלֹא לְעַבֵּר
And we learned from the Jerusalem Talmud that in Nisan and Tishrei they intimidate to sanctify and not to intercalate
(וְהַיְנוּ מִשּׁוּם דְּרֹב אֱלוּל וַאֲדָר אֵין מְעֻבָּר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל).
(which is because Elul and Adar are predominantly not intercalated, as I wrote above).
וְהִנֵּה תַּלְמוּדִין קָאָמַר דִּפְלִיגֵי;
And behold, our Babylonian Talmud states that they dispute;
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּלֹא מַשְׁמַע לְתַלְמוּדִין לְמֵימַר דְּרַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא — דְּהוּא כְּרַבִּי בָּא דִּבִירוּשַׁלְמִי — מַיְירֵי רַק בְּנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי;
and one must say that our Talmud did not deem it plausible to explain that Rav Dimi of Neharde'a — who aligns with Rabbi Ba of the Yerushalmi — referred only to Nisan and Tishrei;
וּלְדֵעָה קַמַּיְיתָא [קַדְמַיְיתָא], דְּהוּא כְּרָבָא וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
and according to the first opinion, which follows Rava and Rabbi Yehudah Nesi'ah —
אִם כֵּן וַדַּאי נַמִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר דְּהָא דִּמְאַיְּמִין לְקַדְּשׁוֹ — הוּא רַק בְּנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי, כְּמוֹ דְּלֹא מוֹקֵי דִּבְרֵי רַב דִּימִי בְּכַהַאי גַּוְנָא.
if so, it is certainly impossible to say that intimidating to sanctify applies only in Nisan and Tishrei, just as it did not establish Rav Dimi's words in such a case.
אֲבָל הָא דִּלְעַבְּרוֹ מְאַיְּמִין וּלְצֹרֶךְ — שַׁפִּיר אִיכָּא לְאוֹקְמֵי רַק בִּשְׁאָר חֳדָשִׁים;
However, that which allows intimidating and acting for a need to intercalate — can nicely be established as applying solely to the other months;
וְזֶה אֵין דֹּחַק כְּלָל, וּכְסְבָרַת הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וְכָךְ יִרְאֶה לוֹ לְהָרַמְבַּ״ם.
and this is not strained at all, matching the logic of the Jerusalem Talmud cited above, and so it appeared to the Rambam.
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵין לָנוּ לַחְפּוֹשׂ הוֹכָחוֹת עַל זֶה בַּתַּלְמוּד, כִּי יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם: "יֵרָאֶה לִי" — מִסְתַּבְּרָא לֵיהּ מִדְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ הָכֵי.
And truly we need not search for explicit Talmudic proofs for this, for it is well known that whenever the Rambam writes "it appears to me" — it represents his own reasoned legal deduction.
וְצָרִיךְ לְעַיֵּן: אִם רַק לְעִנְיַן לְאַיֵּם כָּתַב כֵּן, אֲבָל לְצֹרֶךְ מְעַבְּרִין אַף בְּנִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי — כִּדְעוּלָּא, דְּעִבְּרוּהָ לֶאֱלוּל לְצֹרֶךְ;

And it requires examination: whether he wrote this solely regarding intimidation, while for a communal need they intercalate even in Nisan and Tishrei — like Ulla's account where they intercalated Elul for a need;
אוֹ אַף לְצֹרֶךְ כֵּן, וְכֵן מַשְׁמַע בַּגְּמָרָא דִּלְצֹרֶךְ וּמְאַיְּמִין מַמָּשׁ כְּהָדָדֵי, וְאִם כֵּן וַדַּאי פָּלִיג אַדְּעוּלָּא, וְכִדְאִיתָא כֵּן בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי לְרַבִּי זְעִירָא.

or whether for a communal need it is also restricted, as the Gemara implies that a need and intimidation are equivalent, in which case he definitely disputes Ulla, as stated in the Yerushalmi according to Rabbi Ze'ira.
וַהֲרֵי גַּם רַב דִּימִי פָּלִיג אַדְּעוּלָּא; וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן בָּזֶה.
And indeed Rav Dimi also disputes Ulla; and this requires further analysis.
וְעַיֵּן בְּלֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בְּדִבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם, וְיֵשׁ לְהָשִׁיב הַרְבֵּה עַל דְּבָרָיו;
And see in Lechem Mishneh what he wrote regarding the words of the Rambam, upon which much may be countered;
וּבְיִחוּד יִשּׁוּב הֲלָכָה י״ט, בְּלְקַדֵּשׁ — דְּלָא נָחֵית כְּלָל לְבָאֲרָהּ, וְאֵין צֹרֶךְ;
and especially his resolution of Halakhah 19 regarding sanctification — which he did not descend to clarify adequately, nor is there need;
דְּבְעַצְמוֹ כָּתַב שֶׁדְּבָרָיו דְּחוּקִים, עַיֵּן שָׁם.
for he himself wrote that his words were strained, see there.
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי נִרְאֶה לִי מְרֻוָּח בְּדִבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ״ם, בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִשְׁמַיָּא:
And what I have written appears well-founded in the words of the Rambam, with the assistance of Heaven.

An intercalated year [leap year] — is a year to which they add a month, as explained above.
וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין לְעוֹלָם אֶלָּא אֲדָר, וְעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שְׁנֵי אֲדָרִין: אֲדָר רִאשׁוֹן וַאֲדָר שֵׁנִי.
And they never add any month other than Adar, rendering that year with two Adars: First Adar and Second Adar.
וּמִפְּנֵי מָה מוֹסִיפִין חֹדֶשׁ זֶה? מִפְּנֵי זְמַן הָאָבִיב, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַפֶּסַח בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן,
And why do they add this month? On account of the spring season, so that Passover will fall during that season,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שָׁמוֹר אֶת חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב" — שֶׁיִּהְיֶה חֹדֶשׁ זֶה בִּזְמַן אָבִיב.
as it is stated: "Observe the month of spring" — that this month shall coincide with the spring season.
וְלוּלֵי הוֹסָפַת הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה, הַפֶּסַח בָּא פְּעָמִים בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּפְעָמִים בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
And were it not for the addition of this month, Passover would sometimes occur in the summer and sometimes in the rainy winter.
וְעַל שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים מְעַבְּרִין, וּשְׁלָשְׁתָּן מִדְּאוֹרַיְתָא (תּוֹסָפוֹת סַנְהֶדְרִין דַּף י״א עַמּוּד ב׳):
And based on three signs do they intercalate, and all three are of biblical authority (Tosafot Sanhedrin folio 11b):
עַל הָאָבִיב — שֶׁרָאוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא בִּשְּׁלָה הַתְּבוּאָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב";
on account of the spring grain — when the court saw that the grain had not yet ripened, as it is stated "the month of spring";
וְעַל פֵּרוֹת הָאִילָן — שֶׁלֹּא צָמְחוּ, וְיִתְאַחֵר בִּשּׁוּלָם יוֹתֵר מִזְּמַן הָעֲצֶרֶת, וַעֲצֶרֶת זְמַן הֲבָאַת בִּכּוּרִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חַג הַקָּצִיר בִּכּוּרֵי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ";

and on account of tree fruit — which had not yet sprouted, and whose ripening would be delayed beyond Shavuot, Shavuot being the time for bringing the first fruits, as it is stated: "the festival of the harvest, the first fruits of your labors";
וְעַל הַתְּקוּפָה — שֶׁחִשְּׁבוּ בֵּית דִּין וְיָדְעוּ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה תְּקוּפַת נִיסָן בְּשִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן אוֹ אַחַר זְמַן זֶה,
and on account of the equinox — when the court calculated and knew that the vernal equinox would occur on the sixteenth of Nisan or later,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שָׁמוֹר אֶת חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב" — שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַפֶּסַח בְּחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב;
as it is stated: "Observe the month of spring" — that Passover shall fall within the seasonal month of spring;
וְאִם תִּמָּשֵׁךְ תְּקוּפַת טֵבֵת עַד שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן — לֹא יִהְיֶה יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח בְּחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב שֶׁל תְּקוּפָה (לְבוּשׁ מֵהָרַמְבַּ״ם, וְעַיֵּן הַגָּהוֹת):
(and if the winter season of Tevet extends until the sixteenth of Nisan — the first day of Passover will not fall within the seasonal month of spring (Levush from Rambam, and see glosses).

And this accords with the authority in Sanhedrin (folio 13a) who holds: "the day of the equinox begins the season";

Yet this is difficult: let them make Adar thirty days, and the equinox will arrive on the fifteenth; why then is an entire leap month required?

And one must answer: he holds that the day of the equinox concludes the season, and therefore on the fifteenth it is possible to make Adar thirty days; but on the sixteenth — it is impossible.

Whereas according to the authority who holds the day of the equinox begins the new season — on the sixteenth they make Adar thirty days, and on the seventeenth they intercalate the year.
וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים (תּוֹסָפוֹת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דַּף כ״א עַמּוּד א׳, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "כִּי"),
And some say (Tosafot Rosh Hashanah folio 21a, s.v. "Ki"),

that what Scripture states, "Observe the month of spring" — means: that the solar season of Nisan, called "Aviv," must fall in the month's renewal — meaning when the moon is waxing;

and the moon is called "new" only until the fifteenth of Nisan, whereas from the fifteenth onward it is called "old."
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ, לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יוֹם תְּקוּפָה גּוֹמֵר;
And this also, perforce, follows the authority who holds the equinox day concludes the season;

and even if they make Adar thirty days — so that the equinox falls on the fifteenth; the equinox day concludes the winter, and spring begins only after the fifteenth.

And one must answer: the fact that the Gemara left it unresolved — is either as Tosafot wrote in several places, that it is the Talmud's style to resolve in one tractate what it left unresolved in another;

that we hold like Acherim, that we do not take the equinox of Tishrei into account, etc., see there.
